idea-plugin.description:
Cfml Extra Completion fills gaps in the bundled CFML plugin's code completion. The built-in completion only sees symbols declared in the current file; this plugin adds the project-wide symbols it misses, and stops flagging them as "unresolved". Suggestions are added on top of the built-in CFML completion — nothing is removed or replaced.

Where the symbols come from

  • Variables and functions declared in the nearest Application.cfm, offered in every page under that directory.
  • application.*, session.*, request.* and custom this.* symbols set in the nearest Application.cfc (e.g. from onApplicationStart / onSessionStart).
  • Variables and functions from files pulled in via cfinclude / script include in the current file (followed recursively, cycle-safe).

They complete unscoped or after the matching scope prefix (application., session., request., this.), shown qualified and highlighted to match the built-in.

And for those same symbols

  • Parameter info — function signatures in completion, plus the argument hint (after ( and while typing arguments).
  • Documentation — a function's preceding comment or hint, in the completion doc pane and Quick Documentation (Ctrl+Q).
  • Go to Declaration — Ctrl/Cmd+Click jumps to the declaration, and follows cfinclude paths resolved through a this.mappings alias.
  • No false "unresolved" warnings — the wavy underline is suppressed for symbols we know exist, while genuinely unknown identifiers stay flagged.

Same-file symbols and standard Application.cfc settings are left to the built-in, so nothing is offered twice.

Optional features (off by default, under Settings | Other Settings | Cfml Extra Completion)

  • Resolve ColdFusion mappings (this.mappings) when following cfinclude.
  • Merge Application.cfm / Application.cfc from all ancestor directories, not just the nearest one.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate with the CFML plugin installed and enabled (this plugin builds on it).
